1. CONVENTIONS, RANK AND NORMALIZATION
N=n^D and p=D/2 are used consistently. Positive-start torus edges are counted once in E_a. In each ordinary coordinate rectangle only edges with both endpoints in that rectangle and with no coordinate wrap are retained. Their starting vertices lie in the same rectangle, so a lower bound on a at every rectangle vertex supplies the required lower bound for every retained coefficient. Nonretained edges have nonnegative energy. Thin rectangles and singletons create no negative or missing term.
For each box, sum_R |f|^2 = Var_R(f)+|R||bar f_R|^2. Dividing by N yields exactly ||f||_N^2=N^(-1)sum Var_R+sum |(Pf)_R|^2 with the stated row normalization. There is neither an extra N nor an extra |R| in the penalty. The J nonzero rows of P have pairwise disjoint supports, hence are linearly independent: real scalar rank is J. Directly repeated independent real components give rJ. No physical/color/coexact identification follows. For f=1, energy vanishes and ||P1||^2=1; therefore a penalty K||Pf||^2 can dominate c||f||_N^2 only if K>=c. K=c is sufficient for the construction, without any claim that J is globally optimal.

2. PATH INEQUALITY AND TENSORIZATION
On an l-site path the exact variance identity is l^(-1)sum_{u<v}|f_u-f_v|^2. Telescoping gives |f_u-f_v|^2 <= (v-u)sum_{k=u}^{v-1}|d_k f|^2. At edge k, 1<=k<=l-1, there are k(l-k) crossing pairs, each with v-u<=l. After dividing by l, the coefficient is at most k(l-k)<=l^2/4. This proves the claimed loose but valid path constant. For l=1 both sides are zero.
In the product counting Hilbert space, the averaging projections commute. The orthogonal decomposition into constant/nonconstant tensor factors writes total variance as the sum of squared components indexed by nonempty coordinate subsets S. The sum of fiber variances counts the S component |S| times. It therefore dominates total variance. Applying the path bound on every coordinate fiber and summing produces Var_R <= L^2 E_R^0/4 with no extra D. This also handles side lengths unequal to L and factors of length one. No boundary condition or torus spectral gap was silently used.

3. POINT ISOLATION AND THE ACTUAL MOMENT TAIL
For the proposed split of a box containing z, each x other than z has a unique first coordinate i where x_i differs from z_i and a unique sign there. Earlier coordinates equal z, later coordinates are unrestricted, exactly as the displayed pieces require. Thus the cover is disjoint, exhaustive and rectangular. There are at most 2D+1 nonempty new boxes, hence at most 2D extra boxes. A subsequent distinct marked vertex is not inside an already isolated singleton. Iteration therefore gives J<=J0+2Dm, preserving the side cap. No complexity or logarithmic-depth claim is needed.
If a(x)<h, then (mu/a(x))^p>(mu/h)^p since p>0. Summing over B_h gives m_h(mu/h)^p <= M N, with strict inequality when m_h>0; the weaker displayed inequality is valid for all m_h including zero. This uses the actual a, actual mu and actual critical inverse moment, and remains valid at intermediate coefficient values. It neither rounds a down to 1 nor substitutes a nominal mean. M>=1 automatically for an admissible field by Jensen applied to t^(-p); in particular the constants multiplying max terms are nonnegative. The lower envelope a>=1 makes h=1 harmless because B_1 is empty.

4. GENERAL h AND h=SQRT(mu) BOUND
After all subthreshold vertices are isolated, every nonsingleton rectangle contains only a>=h vertices. If L(h)>=2, the max(1,floor(.)) branch implies L(h)<=sqrt(h)/b, including when the cap n is active. Thus its weighted retained energy is at least 4h Var_R/L(h)^2 >=4b^2 Var_R >=c Var_R. If L(h)=1 all boxes are singletons and every local variance vanishes, so this case needs no false estimate L<=sqrt(h)/b. Summing and using the exact normalization proves (3.1) for every real f, with finite penalty c.
For x=sqrt(h)/b, max(1,floor x)>=x/2 for both x<1 and x>=1. Hence L>=min(n,sqrt(h)/(2b)). Since n/L>=1, ceil(n/L)<=2n/L. Combining gives J0<=(4b)^D max(1,N/h^p); the constant is deliberately loose and survives the n-cap and the floor. Adding 2Dm_h proves (3.2), and the moment tail proves (3.3).
With h=sqrt(mu), N/h^p=N/mu^(D/4). Also m_h<=MN/mu^(D/4). Therefore J<=((4b)^D+2DM)max(1,N/mu^(D/4)). Since mu>=1, replacing mu with 1+mu costs at most 2^(D/4), including the maximum with 1. This is exactly C1 in (3.4). There is no use of a<=2mu here; the upper theorem holds without that additional envelope. The result has mean exponent D/4, not D/2. It is a real positive variable-coefficient result, with a worse observation budget than the original target.

5. ACTUAL TWO-LEVEL FAMILY AND ALL-h ATTACK
For integer s>=2, D>=3, delta=s^(-D)<=1/8, n=A=s^2 and H=s^4. The low set Q has s^D points out of N=s^(2D). Its actual mean is H[1-delta(1-s^(-2))], lying between H/2 and H. Thus a>=1 and a<=H<=2mu. These are admissible actual coefficients even under the original upper envelope.
The inverse moment is exactly (mu/H)^p[(1-delta)+delta(H/A)^p]. Since (H/A)^p=s^D=1/delta, this is (mu/H)^p(2-delta)<2. Jensen gives its lower bound 1. Fixing M=2 for the entire family is valid; M is not secretly growing with s. The upper target estimate follows from N=H^p and mu>=H/2, giving 1<=T_s=max(1,N/(1+mu)^p)<=2^p. The low sites do not violate the moment just because their individual normalized inverse contributions grow: their fraction exactly compensates that growth.
The strategy is explicitly restricted to c=1, an initial partition with every side <=L(h), refinement only, and compulsory separate singleton boxes for all a<h. Arbitrary field-dependent choices of h are covered. For h<=A, sqrt(h)<=s and L(h)<=s, so each initial rectangle contains at most s^D sites. Covering N sites requires at least s^D boxes; refinement cannot reduce the count. For h>A, every point of Q is subthreshold and compulsory singleton isolation alone forces at least s^D final boxes. This includes h=H (strict inequality excludes strong sites but includes Q) and h>H (all sites become marked). Thus no exceptional threshold between A and H, at either endpoint, below 1 after imposing h>=1, or above H evades the dichotomy.
Consequently J/T_s>=s^D/2^p diverges for fixed D,c=1,M=2. It defeats a uniform target-order rank constant in exactly that strategy. At h=A, B_h is empty because the threshold is strict, L=s and the regular grid has (n/s)^D=s^D boxes. The universal lower bound and this attained value imply the minimum actual count is exactly s^D for the regular-grid/isolation construction (and the same minimum over the larger stated class). The proof is about actual counts, not merely minimizing an upper estimate.
Because mu/H is bounded between 1/2 and 1, N/mu^(D/4) lies between s^D and 2^(D/4)s^D. The upper bound's order is attained on this sequence in the defined route. This does not make an unrestricted minimax assertion across all parameters or all rectangle choices; it does rule out a smaller uniform mean exponent loss for this strategy on the displayed family. Fixed c=1 is sufficient to falsify a claim that the strategy works for every c>0. The note does not prove an identically phrased all-c obstruction, nor does it need one.

6. ADAPTED D+1 BOX ESCAPE
Q is one rectangle. Outside Q, the first coordinate outside [0,s-1] places each point in exactly one of the D listed rectangles. Those boxes are nonempty since n=s^2>s. Thus the partition consists of exactly D+1 nonempty disjoint rectangles. Their coordinates fit inside the ordinary fundamental-domain intervals and no wrapping internal edge is required.
All internal starts in a strong box carry H, its longest side is at most n, and H=n^2. The path/product bound gives energy at least 4 Var there. In Q the coefficient A=s^2 and longest side s give the same factor 4. Singleton or thin fiber directions cause no failure of that bound. Dropping interface edges loses only nonnegative energy; the full energy is at least 4 times the sum of variances. The normalized mean identity then proves E_a/N+c||Pf||^2>=c||f||_N^2 for every 0<c<=4. In particular c=1 has rank D+1<=(D+1)T_s. This is a constructive escape at the original order for this family, not just absence of a lower-bound proof. It violates the negative strategy's premises by grouping low sites and using local scales, which is allowed for the unrestricted problem. The constant 4 is a sufficient analytic constant, not a claimed optimal gap or an all-c guarantee.

It is not a no-go for every algorithm with one parameter, for multilevel/local-scale partitions, for arbitrary partitions, or for arbitrary finite penalties. The source explicitly acknowledges these restrictions. A publication title or abstract deleting them would exceed this verdict.
